summary:
Museum of the Abandoned is an interactive, museum-style web app built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, answering the challenge "Abandoned but Not Forgotten."
Space history is full of missions and machines that quietly faded from memory. We wanted to bring them back.
Explore the spacecraft and rovers sent to the Moon, Mars, and beyond, all built on real NASA data and imagery. Meet the explorers that crossed lunar dust and Martian plains, follow their journeys, and see what they left behind.
But reading is only the start. Games and challenges let you test what you've learned, so discovery feels like play.
Our goal is simple: to turn forgotten achievements into fresh discoveries, and to inspire a new generation to look up, stay curious, and dream past the stars.
details:
Museum of the Abandoned is an interactive, educational digital museum that brings the stories of NASA's abandoned and retired space exploration equipment to life. Inspired by the challenge “Abandoned but Not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars,” our project transforms forgotten spacecraft, landers, rovers, and scientific instruments into meaningful stories of human curiosity, scientific discovery, and exploration.

Through an immersive virtual museum, visitors are invited to explore three destinations: the Moon, Mars, and Deep Space. Guided by Dr. Fredrick and an interactive storytelling experience, users discover the missions, technologies, scientific objectives, achievements, and lasting contributions of space exploration hardware that remains on other worlds or in space.

Rather than simply presenting mission facts in conventional slides, Museum of the Abandoned uses character-driven storytelling, mission-specific images, historical evidence, and interactive conversations to make complex space science accessible and engaging, particularly for younger audiences and students.

Each exhibit connects visitors with the real history of NASA missions and explains why the equipment was sent, what it accomplished, and why its legacy still matters. Our project also distinguishes between hardware that physically reached a planetary surface and spacecraft that remained in orbit or deep space, ensuring that the exhibits accurately represent their mission histories.

Our goal is to turn forgotten space technology into a source of inspiration, encourage curiosity about planetary science and engineering, and help the next generation understand that space exploration does not end when a mission is over.

A mission can end. But discovery doesn't have to.

Museum of the Abandoned — Abandoned, but Not Forgotten.
